abenobashi-abeno.scene: Set in an old shopping arcade in Abeno, Osaka, where two kids defend their streets through one alternate world after another.
abenobashi-abeno.tips: Today's Abeno is full of high-rises — go up Abeno Harukas for a view over Osaka. Tennōji Zoo and Tsūtenkaku are nearby.

anohana-chichibu.work: Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day
anohana-chichibu.scene: A coming-of-age story set in Chichibu; the old bridge appears in the opening and many scenes, and the city has worked with the series for years.
anohana-chichibu.tips: The shopping streets near Chichibu Station and Jōrin-ji temple are also locations. The old bridge is pedestrian-only — mind other walkers.

anonatsu-komoro.work: Waiting in the Summer (Ano Natsu de Matteru)
anonatsu-komoro.scene: Over a summer of making a home-made movie, Komoro's station, Kaikoen park and streets become the story's stage.
anonatsu-komoro.tips: Kaikoen, the Komoro Castle site beside the station, is worth a visit; the series displays are in the station and tourist facilities.

atsuhime-edojo.place: Edo Castle site (East Gardens of the Imperial Palace)
atsuhime-edojo.scene: Atsuhime of Satsuma marries into the shogun's family, lives through the end of the shogunate in the Ōoku, and helps bring about the bloodless surrender of Edo Castle.
atsuhime-edojo.tips: The East Gardens are free to enter (closed some days), with the keep foundation and Honmaru site; bags are checked at the gate.

bocchi-shimokitazawa.scene: Socially anxious guitarist Hitori Gotoh joins Kessoku Band in Shimokitazawa, a neighborhood packed with live houses.
bocchi-shimokitazawa.tips: Shimokitazawa is all vintage shops, small theaters and live houses — catching a live show is the most fitting pilgrimage. The lanes are narrow; don't block them for photos.

byousoku-iwafune.scene: In the first episode, "Cherry Blossom", the station where Takaki waits through the heavy snow is Iwafune on the JR Ryōmō Line.
byousoku-iwafune.tips: It is a working station: don't linger on the platform for photos or get in passengers' way. A snowy winter day is closest to the film's mood.

diy-sanjo.scene: High-school girls build things by hand in a DIY club, set in Sanjō, a city famous for blades and metalwork that collaborates with the series.
diy-sanjo.tips: Sanjō is a city of craftspeople — try forging a small knife at a local smithing workshop. Factories are working sites; don't enter without permission.

eupho-uji.scene: The Kitauji High concert band story is set in Uji; the riverside, Uji Bridge and the Mount Daikichi lookout are famous scenes.
eupho-uji.tips: The Uji riverside is a pleasant walk; the Daikichi lookout needs a short climb. The school is modeled on a real high school — don't enter the grounds.

flying-witch-hirosaki.scene: Makoto, a witch in training, moves in with relatives in Hirosaki; the castle town, Mount Iwaki and the apple orchards run through the whole series.
flying-witch-hirosaki.tips: Hirosaki Park's spring blossoms and the town's Western-style buildings make a lovely walk. The homes in the series are ordinary houses — please don't disturb residents.

furinkazan-takeda.scene: The story of Yamamoto Kansuke, strategist to Takeda Shingen; the Takeda residence at Tsutsujigasaki stood where Takeda Shrine is today.
furinkazan-takeda.tips: The original moat and earthworks survive around the shrine; buses run directly from Kōfu Station.

garupan-oarai.scene: The heroines' Ōarai Girls' Academy calls Ōarai its home port; the shopping streets and the torii on the rocks by the sea appear throughout — a model of anime–town collaboration.
garupan-oarai.tips: The shopping streets are full of character standees and tie-in goods; supporting local shops is part of the pilgrimage. The torii stands on rocks — keep away at high tide or in big waves.

glasslip-mikuni.scene: A summer between a girl raised in a glass workshop and a transfer student, set in the seaside town of Mikuni in Sakai, Fukui.
glasslip-mikuni.tips: Mikuni's old streets and shore are good for walking. The nearby Tōjinbō cliffs have no railings — keep well back from the edge.

golden-kamuy-abashiri.scene: In late-Meiji Hokkaido, Abashiri Prison holds a key to the hunt for the hidden gold; the museum's radial cell blocks are the very ones the story draws on.
golden-kamuy-abashiri.tips: The grounds are large with a lot of outdoor walking — dress warmly and watch for ice in winter. It is a historical site, so keep your voice down.

gou-odani.work: Gō: Princesses of the Warring States
gou-odani.scene: The three daughters of Azai Nagamasa and Oichi — Chacha, Hatsu and Gō — were born at Odani Castle, where the drama begins and where they first saw a castle fall.
gou-odani.tips: Odani is a steep mountain castle; the climb takes one to two hours, so wear proper shoes. The museum at the foot explains the Azai family first.

hakuouki-iimoriyama.scene: A story centered on the Shinsengumi, which in its later part follows them to Aizu; Mount Iimori is where the young Byakkotai met their tragic end in the Boshin War.
hakuouki-iimoriyama.tips: The hill has the Byakkotai graves and the unusual Sazaedō hall — please be respectful. The stone steps are steep; a paid escalator is available.

hanasaku-yuwaku.scene: Ohana grows up working at the inn Kissuisō; the spa town is modeled on Yuwaku Onsen outside Kanazawa, which even started holding the series' Bonbori Festival for real.
hanasaku-yuwaku.tips: Yuwaku is a quiet mountain spa — don't wander into inns' private areas for photos. It gets crowded during the autumn Bonbori Festival.

hantsuki-ise.work: Half a Moon Rises in the Sky (Hanbun no Tsuki ga Noboru Sora)
hantsuki-ise.scene: A hospitalized boy and a seriously ill girl, in the author's hometown of Ise.
hantsuki-ise.tips: Combine it with a visit to Ise Jingū. The hospital is modeled on a real one — please don't go in to take photos.

homura-esashi.scene: A drama of the rise and fall of the Ōshū Fujiwara; the Heian-period buildings built for filming became a theme park that still serves many period dramas.
homura-esashi.tips: The park recreates Hiraizumi-style palaces — great for period-style photos. Pair it with Chūson-ji and Mōtsū-ji in Hiraizumi.

homura-kanezawa.scene: Part two of the drama covers the Later Three Years' War, whose final battle was fought at the Kanezawa stockade in Dewa — the foundation of the Ōshū Fujiwara.
homura-kanezawa.tips: The battlefield is now Kanezawa Park and Kanezawa Hachimangū; the nearby museum of the Later Three Years' War explains the battle. Lovely in autumn colors.

hyouka-takayama.scene: The Classics Club's everyday mysteries take place in Kamiyama, modeled on Hida-Takayama, with its old streets, shrines and festivals.
hyouka-takayama.tips: Takayama's old streets are crowded — keep the narrow lanes clear when taking photos. The school is modeled on a real high school; don't enter the grounds.

ieyasu-iga.work: What Will You Do, Ieyasu? (Dōsuru Ieyasu)
ieyasu-iga.scene: After the Honnō-ji Incident, Ieyasu fled from Sakai back to Mikawa over the Iga mountains — the drama's tense "crossing of Iga" passes through this land of ninja.
ieyasu-iga.tips: Iga-Ueno Castle's tall stone walls are striking, and the Iga-ryū Ninja Museum below has live ninja demonstrations.

ieyasu-okazaki.work: What Will You Do, Ieyasu? (Dōsuru Ieyasu)
ieyasu-okazaki.scene: Tokugawa Ieyasu was born at Okazaki Castle in Mikawa, where the drama begins his life of "what will you do?"
ieyasu-okazaki.tips: Okazaki Park around the castle has an Ieyasu museum, and the old Hatchō miso makers nearby offer tours.

initiald-haruna.scene: Mount Akina, where Takumi delivers tofu, is modeled on Mount Haruna; its run of hairpin bends is the series' most iconic setting.
initiald-haruna.tips: These are public roads — never imitate the racing. Lake Haruna and Ikaho Onsen are best enjoyed slowly.

kageki-takarazuka.scene: Girls who dream of becoming stars of a revue company modeled on the Takarazuka Revue; the town and its "Hana no Michi" promenade appear.
kageki-takarazuka.tips: Hana no Michi is a nice walk. Near the theater, please don't follow or photograph performers and students.

kamakuradono-awa.place: Awa (Minamoto no Yoritomo landing site, Kyonan)
kamakuradono-awa.scene: Defeated at Ishibashiyama, Minamoto no Yoritomo fled across the sea to Awa, regrouped here and went on to found the Kamakura shogunate.
kamakuradono-awa.tips: A monument marks Yoritomo's landing on the Kyonan coast; Nihon-ji temple on nearby Mount Nokogiri overlooks Tokyo Bay.

kamakuradono-tsurugaoka.scene: The spiritual center of the Kamakura shogunate; Minamoto no Sanetomo's assassination on its great stone steps is one of the drama's most shocking turns.
kamakuradono-tsurugaoka.tips: Walk from Kamakura Station along the Dankazura approach. New Year and weekends are packed — weekday mornings are best.

kanbei-himeji.scene: Kuroda Kanbei came from Harima and offered Himeji Castle to Hashiba Hideyoshi as his base for conquering western Japan.
kanbei-himeji.tips: Expect queues to climb the keep of this World Heritage castle — go early in high season. Stairs inside are steep and shoes come off.

keion-toyosato.scene: Sakuragaoka High, where the five members of the light music club study, is modeled on the old Toyosato Elementary School in Shiga — especially its staircase with the tortoise-and-hare statues.
keion-toyosato.tips: The old buildings are open to the public with a fan space; they are a town facility, so keep to the opening hours and house rules.

kiminonawa-hidafurukawa.scene: Searching for Mitsuha, Taki comes to Hida and asks around at Hida-Furukawa's station and streets.
kiminonawa-hidafurukawa.tips: The view of trains from the station footbridge is the classic shot — don't block passengers. The Seto River and white-walled storehouses are lovely for a stroll.

kiminonawa-suga.scene: The film's iconic staircase with red railings is the Otoko-zaka steps in front of Suga Shrine.
kiminonawa-suga.tips: This is a quiet residential area: don't linger in the middle of the stairs or make noise. Weekday mornings are quietest.

kirin-ichijodani.scene: After leaving Mino, Akechi Mitsuhide drifted to Echizen and served Asakura Yoshikage; the drama's Echizen years center on Ichijōdani.
kirin-ichijodani.tips: A Sengoku-period street has been reconstructed, giving a feel for a castle town. The site is large — allow half a day.

kiyomori-todaiji.scene: The Taira clashed with the great temples of Nara, ending in Taira no Shigehira burning the city and Tōdai-ji's Great Buddha Hall — a scene the drama portrays.
kiyomori-todaiji.tips: Tōdai-ji's Great Buddha Hall and the deer of Nara Park are musts; feed deer only special crackers, and mind small children — deer can butt.

kunitori-gifu.scene: Two generations of "stealing a province": Saitō Dōsan ruled from Inabayama Castle, which Oda Nobunaga took and renamed Gifu.
kunitori-gifu.tips: Ride the Mount Kinka ropeway up; the keep looks out over the Nōbi plain. Cormorant fishing on the Nagara River is famous in summer.

kyokai-narapark.scene: A girl spirit warrior and a half-yōmu boy fight in Nara and Kashihara; summer scenes around Nara Park appear in the series.
kyokai-narapark.tips: Nara Park's deer are wild animals — feed them only the special deer crackers and watch out for headbutts. The school is modeled on a real high school; don't enter the grounds.

lovelive-uchiura.scene: The nine members of Aqours live in Uchiura, Numazu; Awashima island in the bay and the coastal villages are full of traces of the series.
lovelive-uchiura.tips: Uchiura is a residential fishing village — keep your voice down and don't linger outside homes. Numazu has many tie-in shops; supporting them is part of the pilgrimage.

luckystar-washinomiya.scene: The Hiiragi sisters' family shrine is modeled on Washinomiya Shrine, often seen as one of the starting points of Japan's anime pilgrimage boom.
luckystar-washinomiya.tips: It is a real shrine with normal shrine etiquette. The anime-illustrated ema plaques are a highlight, but please don't read out or photograph other people's wishes.

maruko-shimizu.scene: The author Momoko Sakura's hometown, Shimizu in Shizuoka City, is Maruko's town; a harbor-side mall has a theme attraction for the series.
maruko-shimizu.tips: The attraction is by Shimizu port, where you can also see Mount Fuji across the harbor. Shimizu is known for its tuna dishes.

masamune-zuihoden.scene: One of the highest-rated taiga dramas ever, telling the life of Date Masamune; Zuihōden is his mausoleum.
masamune-zuihoden.tips: The mausoleum sits at the top of stone steps in a cedar grove, with ornate Momoyama-style decoration. It is a grave site — please be quiet.

mayoiga-otsuchi.work: The House of the Lost on the Cape
mayoiga-otsuchi.scene: After the 2011 earthquake, girls start a new life in the "Mayoiga" house of a seaside town modeled on Ōtsuchi, which collaborated with the film.
mayoiga-otsuchi.tips: This area was rebuilt after the disaster; visit with respect. The coastal reconstruction memorials tell the town's story.

nagiasu-kumano.work: Nagi-Asu: A Lull in the Sea
nagiasu-kumano.scene: A story of children from an undersea village and a seaside town; the harbor town on land is modeled on the Kumano area of Mie.
nagiasu-kumano.tips: Kumano's coastline is spectacular — see Shichiri-mihama beach and Shishi-iwa rock. Fishing ports are workplaces; don't get in the way.

naotora-ryotanji.scene: Ryōtan-ji in Iinoya is the family temple of the Ii, and the story of the woman lord Ii Naotora protecting her clan centers on this area.
naotora-ryotanji.tips: The temple garden is celebrated — please be quiet inside. Iinoya-gū shrine and related memorials are nearby.

omohide-yamagata.scene: A Studio Ghibli film: Taeko, a Tokyo office worker, helps with the safflower harvest in rural Yamagata and remembers herself as a fifth-grader.
omohide-yamagata.tips: The Takase area of Yamagata City is the model for the safflower fields, which bloom around July. The fields are private farmland — admire them from the road.

oregairu-chiba.scene: Hikigaya Hachiman is a high-schooler who proudly calls himself a Chiba fan; Chiba City's seafront and streets appear again and again.
oregairu-chiba.tips: The artificial beach at Inage Seaside Park is a fine place for sunset. The series' school is modeled on a real high school — please don't enter the grounds.

praore-nikko.scene: Girls in Nikko form an ice hockey team; the series works with the local pro team, the H.C. Tochigi Nikko Ice Bucks, whose home rink is this arena.
praore-nikko.tips: Catching a live game in season gives the best atmosphere; Tōshō-gū and Kegon Falls fit into the same day.

sanadamaru-numata.scene: Numata Castle, contested by the Sanada and the Hōjō, is a key setting; the dispute became Hideyoshi's pretext for attacking the Hōjō.
sanadamaru-numata.tips: The castle site is now Numata Park, overlooking river terraces; the nearby Nagurumi Castle site belongs to the same story.

sanadamaru-osaka.scene: The title "Sanada Maru" is the outwork Sanada Nobushige built on the south side of Osaka Castle in the Winter Siege; the drama climaxes in the Siege of Osaka.
sanadamaru-osaka.tips: Osaka Castle Park is huge and the keep is a museum; Sankō Shrine south of the castle has sites linked to the Sanada Maru.

sanadamaru-ueda.scene: Ueda Castle, built by Sanada Masayuki, twice repelled great Tokugawa armies — the pride of the Sanada.
sanadamaru-ueda.tips: The Sanada Stone and the West Turret are highlights; spring blossoms and autumn leaves are the best seasons.

sanpei-masuda.scene: The author, Yaguchi Takao, was born in Masuda, Yokote; the clear streams and mountain villages of the series come from his hometown. The museum holds a large collection of his original art.
sanpei-masuda.tips: Masuda is a traditional district of "uchigura" storehouse homes, worth a stroll. Follow the no-photo signs in the original-art galleries.

seiten-fukaya.work: Reach Beyond the Blue Sky (Seiten o Tsuke)
seiten-fukaya.scene: The life of Shibusawa Eiichi, "father of Japanese capitalism", born in Chiaraijima village in Musashi — today's Fukaya.
seiten-fukaya.tips: His family home, Naka-no-ie, is nearby. Fukaya leeks are the local specialty, best in winter.

shinsengumi-mibu.scene: When Kondō Isami and his men came to Kyoto they were quartered in Mibu — first known as the "Mibu rōnin" — and trained and gathered at Mibu-dera.
shinsengumi-mibu.tips: The temple has the graves of Shinsengumi members (Mibuzuka); the nearby former Yagi residence, their headquarters, is open to visitors.

shishi-goryokaku.work: The Age of Lions (Shishi no Jidai)
shishi-goryokaku.scene: The drama depicts the Battle of Hakodate and the short-lived Republic of Ezo; Goryōkaku was the last stronghold of the former shogunate forces.
shishi-goryokaku.tips: Climb the neighboring Goryōkaku Tower to see the star-shaped fort as a whole. It gets crowded in cherry-blossom season — go early.

silver-spoon-obihiro.scene: The story's Ezo Agricultural High School is modeled on the author's alma mater, Obihiro Agricultural High, with its vast pastures and school buildings.
silver-spoon-obihiro.tips: This is a working school: it is not open to casual visitors. View it from the public road, stay out of the pastures and do not photograph students.

slamdunk-kamakurakokomae.scene: The crossing in the anime opening, with the Enoden train passing in front of the sea, has become a must-see for fans from around the world.
slamdunk-kamakurakokomae.tips: It is extremely crowded. Locals repeatedly ask visitors not to stand in the road for photos, not to block trains or cars, and not to make noise near homes.

summertime-tomogashima.scene: The hero returns to "Hitogashima", an island off Wakayama City, for a childhood friend's funeral; the island is modeled on Tomogashima.
summertime-tomogashima.tips: Boats leave from Kada port, with few sailings that stop in bad weather. The island has old gun batteries and hilly paths — bring water.

summerwars-ueda.scene: The hero follows a senior to her family home in Ueda, Shinshū — the Jinnouchi clan, descendants of the Sanada — where a battle across the internet begins.
summerwars-ueda.tips: Ueda Station and the city have displays about the film. The great house is fictional and the hillsides it draws on are private land — please stay out.

supercub-hokuto.scene: Koguma, a high-schooler living alone, buys a used Honda Super Cub, and her days unfold on the mountain roads of Hokuto.
supercub-hokuto.tips: Follow traffic rules on bikes or in cars — the mountain roads are winding. The school is modeled on a real high school; don't enter the grounds.

taiheiki-bannaji.scene: The hero, Ashikaga Takauji, came from the Ashikaga of Ashikaga Estate in Shimotsuke; Bannaji stands on the site of their residence.
taiheiki-bannaji.tips: The temple keeps its moat and earthen walls, the layout of a warrior's residence. The neighboring Ashikaga School is said to be Japan's oldest school.

tamako-demachi.scene: Tamako, daughter of a mochi shop, and everyday life on a shopping street modeled on Kyoto's Demachi Masugata arcade.
tamako-demachi.tips: It's where locals do their shopping — don't block shop fronts for photos. Buying something is the best kind of pilgrimage.

tenchijin-kasugayama.scene: Naoe Kanetsugu grew up at Kasugayama, the castle of Uesugi Kenshin, and much of the drama's first half takes place here.
tenchijin-kasugayama.tips: It is a hilltop castle site — wear good walking shoes. The main enclosure at the top looks out over the Takada plain and the Sea of Japan.

tenchijin-yonezawa.scene: Naoe Kanetsugu serves Uesugi Kagekatsu; after Sekigahara the Uesugi were reduced to Yonezawa, where Kanetsugu spent the rest of his life.
tenchijin-yonezawa.tips: Uesugi Shrine and the Keishōden treasure house on the castle grounds hold the clan's heirlooms. Don't miss Yonezawa beef.

toshiie-kanazawa.scene: Maeda Toshiie took Kanazawa and laid the foundations of the "one-million-koku" Kaga domain; Kanazawa Castle was home to fourteen generations of the Maeda.
toshiie-kanazawa.tips: The castle sits next to Kenroku-en, so visit both together. Its many styles of stone wall earn it the name "museum of stone walls".

truetears-johana.scene: Nanto is home to the studio P.A.WORKS; Jōhana's old streets, station and Hikiyama festival all appear in the series.
truetears-johana.tips: Jōhana is a quiet town of old streets, best explored on foot. Trains on the Jōhana Line are infrequent — check times in advance.

wug-sendai.scene: Seven idols based in Sendai start from nothing; the station plaza and city streets appear again and again.
wug-sendai.tips: The pedestrian decks and shopping arcades around Sendai Station are familiar scenes. Don't block foot traffic when taking photos.

yae-tonami.scene: After defeat in the Boshin War, the Aizu clan was moved to the Tonami Domain on the Shimokita Peninsula; the drama shows its retainers struggling in this cold land.
yae-tonami.tips: Mutsu City has memorials and displays on the Tonami Domain. Public transport on the peninsula is sparse — drive or check bus times in advance.

yae-tsurugajo.scene: Aizu-born Niijima Yae took up a rifle to defend Tsuruga Castle; the drama's siege of Aizu happened here.
yae-tsurugajo.tips: The keep houses a local museum with views over the Aizu basin from the top. The red-tiled keep looks best with spring blossoms.

yattokame-nagoya.scene: Everyday life with Nagoya-loving high-schooler Yatogame and a transfer student, packed with jokes about Nagoya dialect and food.
yattokame-nagoya.tips: Nagoya Castle's restored Honmaru Palace is exquisite; afterwards try the "Nagoya-meshi" from the series — miso katsu, tebasaki and more.

yorimoi-tatebayashi.work: A Place Further than the Universe
yorimoi-tatebayashi.scene: Four girls set out for Antarctica; the hometown and daily life of the lead, Tamaki Mari, are drawn from Tatebayashi.
yorimoi-tatebayashi.tips: The station and the streets and riverbanks of Tatebayashi appear in the series. Tatebayashi is famously hot in summer — guard against heatstroke.

yoshimune-wakayama.scene: Tokugawa Yoshimune, lord of Kishū, became the eighth shogun and launched the Kyōhō Reforms; his home was Wakayama Castle.
yoshimune-wakayama.tips: The keep overlooks Wakayama City and the Kinokawa River; the castle's Momijidani garden is a quiet Japanese garden.

yoshinobu-kodokan.scene: The last shogun came from the Mito Tokugawa and was educated at the domain school Kōdōkan, where he also confined himself after returning power to the emperor.
yoshinobu-kodokan.tips: Kōdōkan is right by Mito Station; in plum season, combine it with Kairakuen garden.

yoshitsune-kurikara.scene: At Kurikara Pass, Kiso Yoshinaka routed the Taira army with his "fire oxen" stratagem; the drama portrays this battle that turned the Genpei War.
yoshitsune-kurikara.tips: The battlefield is in the hills with sloping paths, loveliest when the double cherries bloom in spring. The road is narrow — drive carefully.

yurucamp-motosu.scene: The lakeside where Rin camps alone and meets Nadeshiko in the first episode is Lake Motosu, with its view of Mount Fuji.
yurucamp-motosu.tips: Camp only at proper campsites and take all your rubbish home. Winter by the lake is bitterly cold; never light fires where they're banned.
